body.heading: Small, daily, and defended
paragraphs: Long talks need scheduling and babysitters; ten minutes needs a kettle. A shared cup of tea or coffee at the same point in the day — after dinner, once the house quiets — is a ritual small enough to survive busy seasons, which is exactly when it is needed most.
Defend it lightly: phones elsewhere, television off, door of the day closed. Ten protected minutes beat an hour of half-attention in the same room.

body.heading: What to do with ten minutes
paragraphs: Nothing ambitious. Report the day in headlines, mention one thing that went well, one thing that is on your mind. Some evenings the ten minutes are mostly companionable silence with hot drinks, and those count in full.
A standing question can help on tired days: 'anything you need from me tomorrow?' It is a small question that prevents a surprising number of medium-sized problems.

body.heading: Rituals scale down, not up
paragraphs: On the hardest weeks, the ritual may shrink to five minutes on the doorstep. Shrink it rather than skipping it — a ritual kept small stays alive, and alive rituals can grow again when life allows.
If you live apart for a while — work trips, hospital stays — the ritual travels by phone surprisingly well. Ten minutes is ten minutes; the kettle is optional.

description: Ten protected minutes and a hot drink, at the same time each day, keep a couple connected through the busiest seasons.
